newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Soccer-Tobin to lead "best ever" Australia side against Kiwis.
newsitem.headline: Soccer-Tobin to lead "best ever" Australia side against Kiwis.

text.p: Captain Alex Tobin has described Australia's side to face New Zealand in the Oceania first leg World Cup play-off on Saturday as the best ever.
The veteran Adelaide City defender joins Marconi midfielder Craig Foster as the only home-based players in coach Terry Venables' side against the All Whites.
The winner of the two-leg Oceania play-off will meet an Asian opponent later this year in a final qualifier for a place in the 1998 World Cup in France.
Australia have three players -- Aston Villa goalkeeper Mark Bosnich, Southampton midfielder Robbie Slater and West Ham winger Stan Lazaridis -- with English Premier League experience.
Veteran striker Graham Arnold, who plays for Hiroshima in the Japanese J-League, will lead the attack.
New Zealand will rely heavily on striker Wynton Rufer, whose overseas experience includes playing stints in Germany and Japan.
The second leg will be played in Sydney on July 5.
Defenders: Craig Moore (Glasgow Rangers), Steve Horvat (Hajduk Split), Alex Tobin (Adelaide City, captain)
Midfield: Robbie Slater (Southampton), Craig Foster (Marconi Fairfield), Ned Zelic (Auxerre), Stan Lazaridis (West Ham)
Strikers: Aurelio Vidmar (Tenerife), John Aloisi (Cremonese), Graham Arnold (Hiroshima)
